title: Basel III Post-Crisis Reforms and Stress-Test Regimes

maps.tested: Reported as 'Basel 3 post reform crisis new changes' and as a comparison against earlier accords. One source directs candidates to read the Basel chapters from the GARP book rather than notes.
maps.specifics: Examinable comparisons: pre-SCAP vs. post-SCAP; the standardised vs. internal-models split; output floors; and the Basel 1 / 2 / 2.5 / III progression. The sibling swap across SCAP, EBA and CCAR stress-test regimes, which banks failed which test, base vs. stress scenario requirements, is separately reported.

vardeezReading: ORR-21: untiered in his sheet, but his theme 'Basel III: three components and comparison with Basel I and II' draws on this reading. ORR-22: untiered (tier cell reads 0), but his themes 'Stressed market VaR (calculations)' and 'Basel 2.5 market risk calculation' land squarely here, so treat as high priority. ORR-23: Very Important. ORR-24: untiered, his theme 'LDA approach' is named in no 2026 learning objective and the closest anchor is ORR-24 b (AMA comparison). ORR-17: Important.

selectors.name: Pre-SCAP versus post-SCAP stress testing
selectors.what: Which features belong to pre-SCAP stress testing (mostly single-shock, product or business-unit level, static, not tied to capital adequacy, losses only) and which to post-SCAP (broad macro scenario plus market stress, comprehensive and firm-wide, dynamic and path dependent, an explicit post-stress common equity threshold, losses, revenues and costs).

selectors.name: Standardised versus internal models across accords
selectors.what: Who uses the standardised approach and who uses internal models under each accord (Basel II standardised approach meant for banks whose internal measures were insufficient for IRB; US internationally active banks used IRB), and where the December 2017 reforms removed or constrained internal models (removed for CVA and operational risk, input floors for IRB; the AMA replaced by the SMA).

selectors.name: Output floors, Basel II versus Basel III
selectors.what: The Basel II floor was 80% of Basel I requirements; the Basel III floor is RWA = max(RWA from approved approaches, 72.5% x RWA from the revised standardised approaches only), phased in from 50% in 2022 to 72.5% on 1 January 2027, with the IRB 1.06 scaling factor removed.
selectors.theory: Why a floor was introduced (restore credibility and comparability of RWA, constrain internal models), why the Basel II floor failed (implemented inconsistently), and how the floor binds when model-based RWA is low relative to the standardised RWA.

selectors.name: Basel I, 1996, II, 2.5, III progression
selectors.what: Attaching each change to the right accord: Basel I (risk-based ratios, Tier 1 and total capital over RWA, risk weights, 1995 netting), the 1996 amendment (market risk), Basel II (three pillars, internal risk measures, operational risk capital), Basel 2.5 (stressed VaR, incremental risk charge, comprehensive risk measure), Basel III (CET1, buffers, leverage ratio, LCR, NSFR) and the December 2017 reforms (SMA, SA-CVA, 72.5% floor).

selectors.name: SCAP, CEBS, EBA, CCAR regime comparison
selectors.what: Which regime did what: SCAP 2009 (19 BHCs, 4% Tier 1 common, ten required to raise USD 75 billion), CEBS 2010 (91 banks, seven raised EUR 3.5 billion, Irish banks passed then needed EUR 24 billion), EBA 2011 (90 banks, 5% Tier 1 common, eight raised EUR 2.5 billion, Basel II weights) and CCAR 2011 (published only the macro scenario); which banks failed, base versus stress disclosure, which risk weights.

selectors.name: Basel III capital components and ratios
selectors.what: Basel III capital definitions and minimums: Tier 3 eliminated, Tier 1 split into CET1 and Additional Tier 1, CET1 at least 4.5%, Tier 1 at least 6%, total capital at least 8% of RWA.

selectors.name: Basel III capital buffers
selectors.what: The Basel III buffers and their sizes: capital conservation buffer 2.5%, G-SIB surcharge 1 to 3.5%, countercyclical buffer 0 to 2.5%, and the extra capital they add above the minimum.

selectors.name: Stressed VaR and Basel 2.5 market risk charge
selectors.source: Vardeez: 'Stressed VaR calculation; Basel 2.5 market risk calculation'
selectors.what: Basel 2.5 market risk capital = max(VaR(t-1), mc x average VaR) + max(SVaR(t-1), ms x average SVaR), with multipliers of at least 3, compared with the pre-2.5 charge max(VaR(t-1), m x average VaR).

notSelected: ORR-21 g (Basel II operational risk BIA, standardised and AMA calculations) and h (Solvency II), ORR-22 h (post-crisis legislative and regulatory reforms), ORR-23 a (motivations for the December 2017 reforms beyond the direction of change in S2 and S3), ORR-24 a (the SMA calculation: BI, BIC, loss component, ILM) and c (operational loss data criteria) carry no shape, no Map point and no Vardeez pointer, and the SMA versus AMA pointer on ORR-24 b is covered only as the removal of internal models in S2.
